questions.question: Why does the sky look blue?
questions.explanation: The text explains Rayleigh scattering — blue waves scatter more strongly.

questions.question: What does Gladstone notice in Homer?
answers: The absence of a word for blue
Hundreds of descriptions of the sky
questions.explanation: Gladstone counts the colours in Homer — blue does not occur.

questions.question: Who does the text mention when discussing the hard problem of consciousness?
questions.explanation: Feynman returns to humility in the face of what we don't understand.

questions.question: What do the Himba do differently from Europeans?
answers: They see shades of green better
They only see in black and white
questions.explanation: The Himba point out different shades of green faster.

questions.question: What question does Feynman ask the waitress?
answers: How do you know the sky is blue?
questions.explanation: He asks: how do you know — and the waitress shrugs.
